questions.prompt: How does DNS round robin spread the load?
options: The TTL is set to zero
A name has several A records, and the server rotates their order so clients pick different ones first
The server sends each packet to a different host

options: The attack traffic is split across every site, so no single server is overwhelmed

questions.prompt: A user in Tokyo and one in Paris look up the same CDN name and get different addresses, each near them. What's happening?
options: Split horizon based on job title
Geo-DNS: the authoritative server answers based on where the resolver is
